messages:
alice_corp: Hey team — starting ~15:23 UTC we started seeing a flood of 429s for our production tenant. Endpoints: POST /v1/generate (stream) and POST /v1/embeddings. Errors show up in app logs as 429 Too Many Requests, clients report no Retry-After header. Can someone help triage?

support_jen: Sorry about that — can you paste a raw request/response (headers) and a sample request-id? Also are these coming from a cron/worker or user traffic?

alice_corp: sample response below (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2023 15:23:18 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 87
X-Request-Id: r-0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1705123460
# No Retry-After header present in several responses we captured
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "Too many requests" }
```
Traffic pattern: mix of user-triggered streaming calls and a batch of small embedding calls from a worker every minute.

sre_marc: thanks — two likely vectors: 1) rolling-window RPM hit, 2) synchronized minute-boundary batch from worker causing a sharp spike. Do you have metrics for requests/min over the past 5m and concurrent streams?

alice_corp: spikes show ~650 req/min at peak (we were expecting 500 RPM limit). Concurrent streams ~40 on v1/generate. Worker runs every 60s, 50 parallel embedding requests launched at once.

sre_marc: yep that explains it — minute-aligned worker + concurrent streams -> short hot spike above RPM. Our rate limiter is a rolling 60s window but upstream proxies can still send bursts that exhaust per-tenant slots quickly. Quick mitigations: 1) stagger the worker (random jitter), 2) reduce parallelism, 3) add client-side exponential backoff with jitter.

eng_sam: adding: for streaming endpoints we sometimes undercount tokens vs requests — if the worker uses many short streams that all open concurrently, you get inflight slot occupancy. Can you share tenant id so we can check server-side telemetry? Also share any client retry logic (we've seen retry amplification from sync retries).

alice_corp: tenant_id: tenant-alice-01. Client retry: naive immediate retry on 429, no jitter.

eng_sam: immediate retries are likely amplifying. Please switch to exponential backoff with jitter (example):
```
retry_delay = base * (2 ** attempts) + random(0, jitter_ms)
# base ~ 200ms, max ~ 20s
```
Also prefer 429 Retry-After when present; our gateway sets it for some rate limits but not all internal throttles.

pm_nina: short-term option: we can issue a temporary burst allowance for tenant-alice-01 to smooth this while you deploy staggered workers. That buys ~10-30s of headroom. Would you like that?

alice_corp: yes please — that would help while we patch client logic. Thanks.

sre_marc: I'm kicking off the telemetry check now. Commands I ran: `kubectl logs -l app=edge-proxy --since=5m | grep tenant-alice-01` and queried metrics: `sum(rate(requests_total{tenant="tenant-alice-01"}[1m])) by (endpoint)`. I see the 50->0 spike pattern from the worker at minute boundaries.

eng_sam: opened an internal bug to add server-side protection against synchronous retry amplification on streaming endpoints (link: internal/RED-3201). In the meantime, change worker to randomized schedule: `cron: "*/1 * * * *"` -> add jitter with a random sleep up to 30s.

support_jen: I've requested a temporary burst_quota for tenant-alice-01 (ticket #SUP-1829). Also added guidance to the customer: jitter + backoff + reduce parallel embedding concurrency (we recommend <=10 parallel for that worker).

deploy_bot: edge-batcher canary patch deployed at 1705123475 (batch smoothing enabled for 1 tenant).

alice_corp: applied client backoff and added 0-30s jitter to worker, dropped embedding concurrency to 8. Replaying now. Will report back in ~2m.

sre_marc: monitoring looks better — peak RPM down to ~420, X-RateLimit-Remaining no longer hitting 0. Keep an eye for residual retries.

alice_corp: confirmed — errors dropped to <1% of prior rate. Thanks everyone for the quick help :thumbsup:

support_jen: great to hear. We'll keep the burst quota for 1 hour while you validate. If you want, we can schedule a follow-up to review longer-term config and batching options.

alice_corp: yes please — can we do a 30-min sync tomorrow to go over batching & streaming best practices?

pm_nina: scheduled: Tue 09:30 UTC — invite sent.

end of thread
